person: New parent in the United States, partner/co-parent household
situation: A first-time mother notices yellowish crust and liquid around the umbilical stump during every diaper change and is overwhelmed with anxiety, unable to distinguish normal from dangerous.
trigger: Yellow discharge visible at every diaper change; parent's anxiety is already elevated (describes 'everything has been giving me anxiety').
context: FTM (first-time mother); baby otherwise healthy; no fever, no redness spreading to abdomen. Parent has been told 'dry care' but doesn't know what that means in practice.
behaviour: Posted detailed description to r/newborns seeking reassurance
Described baseline anxiety state ('everything has been giving me anxiety')
constraint: No practical visual guide for what normal vs abnormal cord healing looks like; clinical advice is abstract.
thought: This must be an infection — yellow crust and liquid can't be normal.
fear: Missing a real infection while being told 'it's fine' by everyone.
emotional_stake: Baseline anxiety from new motherhood amplified by every visual cue that looks abnormal.
exact_language: Every time I change her, there's dried yellow crust/liquid around her umbilical stump area...this is my first baby and everything has been giving me anxiety.
desired_change: A clear visual guide showing 'this is normal, this is when to call' with photos or illustrations.

evidence_source.excerpt: Every time I change her, there's dried yellow crust/liquid around her umbilical stump area...this is my first baby and everything has been giving me anxiety.
evidence_source.context: FTM describing hypervigilant monitoring; community confirmed normal.
